dimension_justifications.soundness: The manuscript gives self-contained assumptions and short proofs for T1--T3, and it carefully limits transfer beyond those assumptions. The snapshot's claim map nevertheless labels C-THEORY-001--003 as pending independent audit, so this is not an excellent-level verification package.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The local theorem statements and scope caveats are legible, but the paper never makes its central unifying object operational: the announced intervention block D is not connected to the three results. The title and motivating framing also suggest a broader convex-dynamics/unlearning account than the three disjoint theory statements substantiate.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The verified contribution is a cautious colocation of elementary product/contraction statements with unusually explicit non-transfer caveats. In the current presentation, however, the manuscript does not establish a distinctive unifying theorem, setting, or consequence that would make the collection a sufficiently clear ICLR contribution.

paper_summary: This theory-only manuscript presents: a fixed-quadratic matrix-product and log-remainder identity (T1), full-norm clean-tail contraction under smooth strong convexity plus a conditional directional refinement (T2), and an affine scalar conditional-mean product law (T3). It explicitly makes no empirical, deployment, nonlinear-SGD, or real-noise claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: A reader can directly inspect three compact formal statements and their proofs, while the abstract, theorem follow-up text, limitations, and claim map consistently state that their conclusions do not transfer automatically to nonlinear SGD, logistic training, neural networks, or deployment.
strengths: The abstract is unusually disciplined: it states the exact regimes of T1--T3 and explicitly disclaims empirical and deployment claims.
T2 clearly separates the full-parameter contraction statement from the stronger directional statement and states the invariant-subspace requirement before the proof.
The prose after each theorem explains a concrete non-implication, helping prevent common overreadings of the equations.
The PDF is readable at normal scale, has consistent theorem hierarchy and equation numbering, no visible clipping, and remains comfortably within the stated page limit.
questions: What is the single formal definition of a training-path intervention in this paper, and how does D in Section 2 instantiate in T1, T2, and T3?
Are T1--T3 intended as three separate illustrative abstractions, or as components of one formal account? If the latter, what proposition or formal mapping relates them?
What does the planned training-visible enable policy do operationally, and why is that future policy the relevant falsification path for these three particular statements?

issues.location: Title; Abstract; Section 1, paragraphs 1--2; Section 2; Sections 3.1--3.3
issues.observed_evidence: The introduction frames one question about changing an objective along a trajectory, and Section 2 defines a clean objective A and intervention block D. But T1 is a fixed quadratic from t=0, T2 only specifies switching to L_A at s without defining the preceding intervention dynamics, and T3 is a generic scalar recursion. D is not used in any theorem, and no formal relation connects the three state spaces or conclusions.
issues.why_it_matters: A reader cannot reconstruct the paper's central object or decide whether the contribution is one intervention theory or three independent reminders about products. This weakens evaluability and makes the connection to the title and unlearning motivation appear asserted rather than demonstrated.
issues.required_fix: Add a concise formal bridge and a three-row scope table. For each theorem, state the state variable, active objective/recursion before and after the putative intervention, the exact role of s and D, the quantity that contracts, and the non-covered regime. If no common formal model is intended, say explicitly that the paper is a collection of separate abstractions and revise the identity claim accordingly.
issues.verification_test: A reader unfamiliar with the project should be able to fill in, from the introduction and scope table alone, how D enters each theorem or identify it as intentionally absent, then correctly distinguish the three conclusions without consulting the proofs.
issues.evidence_needed: No new empirical evidence is required; the existing formal scope must be made explicit and internally consistent.

issues.location: Title; Abstract, sentences 1--3; Introduction, lines 38--51; Sections 4--7
issues.observed_evidence: The title promises Training-Path Dependence in Bounded Convex Dynamics, while T3 concerns an affine scalar stochastic recursion rather than a convex dynamical system. The opening invokes attribution and unlearning, whereas the body repeatedly says that no empirical or deployment claim is made and that T2 is not an arbitrary-neural-network unlearning guarantee. The abstract supplies these caveats, but the headline framing still overstates the common domain of the results.
issues.why_it_matters: The framing initially leads a conference reader to expect a theory of a concrete training intervention or an unlearning-relevant mechanism. Discovering instead three narrowly scoped, disconnected statements changes how novelty and significance are assessed; caveats placed later cannot fully repair an imprecise paper identity.
issues.required_fix: Retitle and rewrite the first introductory paragraph to name the actual evidence level and shared mathematical content. Either remove bounded convex dynamics and the unlearning-forward framing, or introduce a precise common convex-dynamics model that genuinely contains all stated results. Make the abstract's theory-only boundary the first-order identity rather than a late qualification.
issues.verification_test: Blind-read the revised title, abstract, and first two introduction paragraphs without the rest of the paper. They should correctly predict that the manuscript contains three scoped formal results, that T3 is not a convex optimization theorem, and that there are no empirical or deployment findings.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is required for truthful reframing; a broader title would require a formal unification or evidence that supports it.

issues.location: Section 4, Empirical status and falsification path; Reproducibility Statement
issues.observed_evidence: Section 4 introduces a training-visible enable policy, natural human-label noise, a clean benign-hard cohort, an event schema, and forbidden-field checks, but none is defined in the manuscript. The frozen snapshot includes only a registry entry marking PLAN-ENABLE-001 as planned, not execution-ready, and not run.
issues.why_it_matters: The paragraph consumes the sole empirical-status section yet does not let a standalone reader understand what future intervention would be tested or what proposition would be falsified. Its unexplained operational vocabulary reintroduces the appearance of an undeclared method.
issues.required_fix: Either replace the paragraph with a two-sentence, plainly defined future-work statement, or add a compact operational definition of the policy, the two scenarios, the decision-time information restriction, and which theorem-boundary each test probes. Keep all language explicitly prospective.
issues.verification_test: A reader can state the future policy's input, decision, prohibited information, and the relation of a positive or negative result to T1--T3 using only the revised manuscript.
issues.evidence_needed: No execution is needed for a clear planned-work description; results would be needed only to make empirical claims.

issues.observed_evidence: The main argument contains three dense theorem/proof blocks and no figure or table. PDF page 3 has substantial unused lower-page space after the conclusion, while the reader must infer the differences among fixed-quadratic terminal error, clean-tail full-norm return, and scalar mean contraction from prose distributed across the document.
issues.why_it_matters: The equations themselves are readable, but the absence of a compact comparison visual amplifies the central scope confusion and makes the many caveats harder to retain.
issues.required_fix: Use available main-text space for a non-evidentiary scope matrix or simple schematic with columns for model, assumptions, state/target, exact conclusion, role of exposure, and excluded transfer. Do not depict it as experimental evidence.
issues.verification_test: After viewing the table or schematic, a reader should correctly answer which result is exact versus bounded, which concerns a norm versus a scalar expectation, and which one requires invariant-subspace structure.
issues.evidence_needed: None; this is a presentation-only addition derived from the stated theorems.

ethics_concerns: No current human-subject or dataset experiment is reported. The manuscript appropriately notes that any future policy must respect data-use conditions and must not use protected, test, clean, or oracle labels at decision time.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control, using only the specified frozen submission snapshot and bundled rubric.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A revised self-contained paper identity and scope mapping that makes the relation, or intentional non-relation, among T1--T3 immediately evaluable.
A title and introduction whose stated domain exactly matches the theory-only evidence.
For a score above 6, evidence of a nontrivial unifying formal result or a carefully executed empirical test tied to a stated claim would be needed.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A proof audit finding that any of T1--T3 fails under its printed assumptions.
Evidence that the planned policy terminology or historical numerical material is being implicitly used to support a current empirical or deployment claim.
A revised framing that broadens the claims to nonlinear SGD, unlearning, or real-noise settings without new supporting evidence.
review_limitations: I assessed only the frozen snapshot and did not inspect repository history, prior reviews, author plans, external literature, or external experiment artifacts.
This is primarily a clarity and presentation review; I did not conduct a full independent mathematical proof audit.
